newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Mexican leader to seek closer ties with Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Mexican leader to seek closer ties with Argentina.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said he will seek a political and economic alliance with Argentina in order to give the two countries a bigger say in international affairs.

In an interview published on Sunday by the Buenos Aires daily Clarin, Zedillo said he will propose "a political and economic alliance" to President Carlos Menem when he arrives late on Monday in Argentina for a three-day visit.

"We are intermediate countries in the concert of nations and we may be weak in front of the powerful," Zedillo said. "But if we can harmonise our views in multilateral form and in our bilateral relations, I think it will be in our mutual benefit."
The two leaders were attending a regional summit in Chile over the weekend.

Mexico, a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) with the United States and Canada, has in the past expressed interest in a free trade pact with Mercosur, the customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
But in the interview he said an agreement with Argentina should take precedence over a deal with Mercosur.
Trade between the two countries this year was $520 million, with a $140 million surplus for Mexico.
